technical_issues.issue: 'A very high altitude would yield low resolution images which is also desirable' – contradiction; low resolution is undesirable for reef imaging.
RAAN of 27.33° claimed to 'indicate the location of the launch facility'; Kourou is at ~52°W and RAAN is not set by launch-site longitude.
Contradictory paragraph: satellite 'without thrusters' yet discusses choosing uncontrolled descent, then restates it has no thrust capability; drag-sail sentence is incomplete.
Wikipedia used as a source, which the task explicitly disallows; references lack titles/authors/access dates.
Claim that vertical inclination 'maintains a significant contact for the vast majority of passes' is vague and unsupported; access table shows duplicated access number 13.

overall: A well-motivated Australian reef-monitoring CubeSat-style mission with sound SSO selection, STK access analysis and EOL planning. Main weaknesses are internal contradictions, a questionable RAAN justification, missing STK files, and sub-professional referencing (Wikipedia, bare URLs) and figure/table labelling.

feedback.summary: You presented a well-motivated Australian reef-monitoring CubeSat mission with a sound sun-synchronous orbit choice, STK access analysis and drag-sail EOL plan. The introduction is strong, but internal contradictions (altitude vs resolution, thrusters at EOL), an incorrect RAAN justification, missing STK scenario files and sub-professional referencing (Wikipedia, bare URLs) held the report back.
next_steps: Fix internal contradictions: clarify that low resolution is undesirable for reef imaging, and rewrite the EOL section so the thruster/descent discussion and drag-sail sentence are consistent and complete.
Replace Wikipedia with primary sources and format all references consistently (authors, titles, dates); number and caption all figures and tables.
Attach your STK scenario files and access reports in an appendix, and add a quantitative recap (orbit elements, access statistics) to strengthen the conclusion.
